<div class="toolbox-kind">Resource · verified 2026-10-04</div>

## Choose the source

| Need | Source | Useful choices |
|---|---|---|
| Global locator or thematic map | Natural Earth | 1:110m, 1:50m or 1:10m country polygons |
| European statistical map or multilingual country attributes | Eurostat GISCO | 1:60m to 1:1m, EPSG:4326/3035/3857 |

These are cartographic geometries. Do not use them for cadastral or high-precision boundary analysis.

## Natural Earth

Natural Earth is public domain and offers three deliberately generalized scales. Use 1:110m for a small world map, 1:50m for a larger regional/world map and 1:10m only when the display needs the extra detail.

### R

```r
library(sf)
library(rnaturalearth)

sf <- ne_countries(
  scale = 110,
  type = "countries",
  returnclass = "sf"
)

sf |>
  select(adm0_a3, name, sovereignt, continent, geometry)
```

### Python

```python
import geopandas as gpd

url = (
    "https://naciscdn.org/naturalearth/110m/cultural/"
    "ne_110m_admin_0_countries.zip"
)

gdf = gpd.read_file(url)
gdf = gdf[["ADM0_A3", "NAME", "SOVEREIGNT", "CONTINENT", "geometry"]]
```

The Python URL is the official Natural Earth CDN. The verified 1:110m file contains 177 features in EPSG:4326.

Natural Earth countries show de facto control by default. For disputed boundaries or a required editorial point of view, inspect its boundary and point-of-view layers rather than treating the default as politically neutral.

## Eurostat GISCO

GISCO is particularly convenient for European maps because it provides generalized geometries with English, French and German names plus ISO-style identifiers. In R, prefer `giscoR`; it exposes the source choices directly and manages downloads and caching.

### R with `giscoR`

```r
library(dplyr)
library(giscoR)
library(sf)

sf <- gisco_get_countries(
  year = 2024,
  resolution = 10,
  epsg = 4326,
  spatialtype = "RG",
  ext = "gpkg"
) |>
  select(CNTR_ID, ISO3_CODE, NAME_ENGL, NAME_FREN, NAME_GERM, geometry)

gisco_attributions()
```

`resolution` accepts 1, 3, 10, 20 or 60 million. Use `spatialtype = "LB"` for label points or `"BN"` for boundary lines; `country` and `region` can limit a polygon request. For European area calculations, request `epsg = 3035` directly rather than reprojecting a less suitable web/display geometry later.

The tested call returned 263 features in EPSG:4326. `giscoR` caches downloads by default; still save the selected geometry in the project when exact reproducibility matters.

### Direct file access

Direct URLs remain useful in Python or when the exact distributed file should be visible in the workflow.

This example uses 2024 country regions optimized for 1:10 million in WGS84:

```text
https://gisco-services.ec.europa.eu/distribution/v2/countries/geojson/CNTR_RG_10M_2024_4326.geojson
```

#### R

```r
library(sf)

url <- paste0(
  "https://gisco-services.ec.europa.eu/distribution/v2/countries/geojson/",
  "CNTR_RG_10M_2024_4326.geojson"
)

sf <- st_read(url, quiet = TRUE) |>
  select(CNTR_ID, ISO3_CODE, NAME_ENGL, NAME_FREN, NAME_GERM, geometry)
```

#### Python

```python
import geopandas as gpd

url = (
    "https://gisco-services.ec.europa.eu/distribution/v2/countries/geojson/"
    "CNTR_RG_10M_2024_4326.geojson"
)

gdf = gpd.read_file(url)
gdf = gdf[
    ["CNTR_ID", "ISO3_CODE", "NAME_ENGL", "NAME_FREN", "NAME_GERM", "geometry"]
]
```

The verified file contains 263 EPSG:4326 features. Change the year, scale or projection only after confirming the filename in the [GISCO countries distribution API](https://gisco-services.ec.europa.eu/distribution/v2/countries/).

The filename components are explicit:

```text
CNTR_RG_10M_2024_4326.geojson
     │  │   │    └─ CRS
     │  │   └────── reference year
     │  └────────── map scale (1:10 million)
     └───────────── region polygons
```

For analysis in Europe, prefer the equal-area EPSG:3035 version. For web/display exchange, EPSG:4326 GeoJSON is usually convenient.

## Save a project copy

External sources can update independently. Save the actual input and record its source/version instead of downloading silently on every render.

```r
library(here)

raw_dir <- here("input", "raw")
dir.create(raw_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

st_write(
  sf,
  file.path(raw_dir, "countries_gisco_2024_10m.gpkg"),
  quiet = TRUE
)
```

```{python}
#| eval: false
from pathlib import Path

raw_dir = Path("input/raw")
raw_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
gdf.to_file(raw_dir / "countries_gisco_2024_10m.gpkg", driver="GPKG")
```
